criteria.response_evidence: The applicable classification is NG (no grade), and the instructor should record NG instead of the proposed NC. NC applies when a student fails the subject. Here, the instructor has confirmed passing class standing and accepted the documented illness as a valid reason for missing the final examination, satisfying the stated NG conditions. The missing examination alone does not establish failure in the subject.
criteria.source_basis: Sec. 3.2.1 (NC = failure) and Sec. 3.2.2 (NG = passing standing missed final exam/requirements due to illness or other valid reasons), Art. 5, CNU Student Manual (2018).
criteria.reason: The response correctly identifies NG rather than NC, maps NC to failure, and applies the passing-standing/illness facts to NG without asserting that a missing exam alone means failure.

criteria.response_evidence: NG may be removed only after compliance with the requirements within the one-year reglementary period. If the requirements are not completed within the specified time, NG becomes a permanent entry in the Official Transcript of Records. The provision also requires a student who obtained NG to re-enroll the subject until a passing grade is earned; it does not specify how re-enrollment is coordinated with timely completion. It does not provide for automatic conversion of NG to NC.
criteria.source_basis: Sec. 3.2.2.a (removal within one-year reglementary period after compliance) and Sec. 3.2.2.b (permanent transcript entry; re-enroll until passing grade), Art. 5, CNU Student Manual (2018).
criteria.reason: States the one-year removal period, the permanent transcript consequence, and the re-enrollment obligation, while explicitly avoiding the prohibited 'automatic NC conversion' inference and flagging the re-enrollment/period ambiguity.

criteria.response_evidence: This review recommends the policy-supported classification; the instructor/professor retains sole authority to determine and give the grade. It neither awards a numerical passing grade nor waives the outstanding examination. No numerical course grade can be calculated from the supplied facts.
criteria.source_basis: Section 4 ('The instructor/professor has the sole authority to determine and give grades to his/her students'), Art. 5, CNU Student Manual (2018).
criteria.reason: Correctly bounds the review as identifying the supported classification while reserving grade-giving to the instructor and declining to post a numerical grade from the incomplete data.

judgment.overall_reason: The response satisfies all three criteria: correct NG classification, correct completion consequences without automatic-conversion inference, and correct authority boundary with no unsupported numerical grade. No substantive error or omission is present.

reference_concern.detail: No conflict between the supplied policy and the reference; both draw from the same source language, and the reference itself flags the re-enrollment/period ambiguity that the original response also acknowledges.
